title: Claude Code settings.local.json Secrets: GitHub, Docker Hub
content_md: TL;DR 31,088 secrets, 5,343 valid: GitGuardian found 31,088 distinct secrets in Claude Code’s .claude/settings.local.json on public GitHub, across 23,276 repositories, and 5,343 of them worked when we detected them. “Yes, and don’t ask again” writes the key: approving a command permanently makes Claude Code save an allow rule that is the command string itself, API key included, in the project’s settings file. One valid token in 559 Docker image tags: COPY . . ships the working tree, not the git index, so 613 secrets, 99 valid, reached public Docker Hub images; one valid Cloudflare API token appears in 559 tags. 92% drop from the April 2026 peak: monthly leaks in settings.local.json peaked at 12,535 occurrences in April 2026, then fell to 959 by October, and we do not yet know what changed. I have been doing research for a long time, and a good sign that you are working on something worth doing is that other researchers are working on the same topic. It can feel frustrating at first, but it is great. This one first occurred to me in early 2026, while I was doing research on n8n and kept finding n8n API keys inside Claude Code settings files. On November 5, Apiiro published their analysis of .claude/settings.local.json . Here are the results I had planned to release in the State of Secrets Sprawl 2027, refreshed to this week, with what only continuous monitoring can see.
